caption: The drawing shows three views of an ornately detailed chair: a front view, a side view, and a plan (top) view of the seat and stretcher. The front view displays the high back of the chair, which is rectangular but with a curved and carved upper section featuring elaborate floral or scrollwork patterns. The seat is rectangular, and the lower front part of the chair includes more intricate scrolling designs between the legs. The legs are turned and ornamented, with spherical elements and decorative bands, and are connected by stretchers, one of which features a small finial in the center. The side view shows the chair’s tall back inclined slightly, the shape of the legs, and the placement of the stretcher near the floor. The plan view shows the chair from above, illustrating the shape of the seat and how the stretchers connect the legs. The drawing is done in black ink or pencil on a beige or light tan colored paper. Dimensions are marked on the drawing; for example, the seat is shown as 18 1/2 inches wide and 14 1/2 inches deep, and the chair back reaches 51 1/2 inches in height. There is a label identifying the object as a "CHAIR, LIVING ROOM AT EDENTON, N.C., BROOKLYN MUSEUM," and a scale in inches is provided. The drawing includes notes such as "PLAN OF SEAT," "PLAN OF STRETCHER," "FRONT VIEW," and "SIDE VIEW," as well as the name "B. HOLST-GRUBBE" at the bottom left.
title: Chair
